_doc: The rclone operations the fleet declares, as data. Same shape and the same rule as drive-mirror-jobs.json: an operation is declared here or it does not exist, and `delete` is DECLARED PER JOB and is never a switch in the UI — it is the one flag that loses data, so it has to be a written decision, not a tap.
_doc_kinds: kind is the rclone verb. `mount` is how the fleet actually uses rclone today — the photoprism sidecar holds oracle_s3:my-photos on the VM — and `sync` / `copy` / `check` are the transfer verbs the RcloneRPC engine maps to once the APK carries a native rclone library (a build-system change in the GitHub Actions workflow, declared like every other native dependency; the previous run of this ticket tried to cross-compile the binary in a container and that is not how this fleet builds).
_doc_fleet_side: Every job here is fleet-side today: the phone has no rclone binary, so it can only READ the declared state, not run it. The section says that out loud instead of rendering an empty list (rules of #292).
_doc_secret_rule: A job must not carry a credential. Remotes authenticate per the auth source named in drive-remotes.json; a job never carries a token.

jobs.name: Photoprism originals mount
jobs.destination: /opt/containers/photoprism/originals (oci-apps, bind mounted ro into the photoprism app)
jobs.schedule: always-on rclone sidecar (photoprism_rclone container, network_mode host, healthcheck ls /data)
jobs.notes: The fleet's only declared rclone operation. Read-only by construction: VFS cache full, --allow-other, mounted from the sidecar's environment so the S3 keys never enter a command line.
